svg.text: HOW TO MAKE IT AND HOW IT FITS

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Turn to 44 mm diameter x 18 mm; bore 16 mm, a close slide fit.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Face both ends square; the hammer's top face hits the underside.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Slide it on the upper rod from the top so its underside is

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: 711.5 mm above the rod shoulder. With the 136.5 mm hammer

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: this gives the 575 mm free drop. Set it with a rule and check

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: the drop with the hammer on a flat plate standing for the anvil.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Clamp it there and drill 6 mm straight through collar and rod

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: together, at mid-height (720.5 mm above the shoulder).

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Drive in a 6 x 40 mm spring steel roll pin; its ends sit just

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Check: the free drop is 575 mm, within 2 mm; the collar does not

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: move when the hammer is jerked up against it.
